item.title: Nationwide ground stop scrambles weekend sports travel
item.description: A four-hour FAA ground stop forced teams across college football, the NBA, NHL and women’s basketball to improvise. No. 19 Mississippi’s game at Oklahoma moved to Sunday; Auburn and Purdue switched to buses; several kickoffs shifted; and Cleveland planned to land only eight hours before facing Dallas.

item.title: IIHF challenges ruling that reinstated Russian teams
item.description: The International Ice Hockey Federation challenged a Court of Arbitration for Sport order admitting Russian teams to five tournaments, according to The Athletic and TSN. The challenge reportedly says two panel members failed to disclose Russian ties. Canada also says it will bar Russian participants from the World Juniors.

item.title: NC State brings Philip Rivers home as head coach
item.description: NC State hired former Wolfpack and NFL quarterback Philip Rivers to lead its football program. Rivers set ACC career records for passing yards, completions and attempts from 2000–03, but enters the college job without prior coaching experience at that level. The university plans to introduce him Monday.

item.title: Alvarez and Crow-Armstrong sweep unanimous MLB MVP votes
item.description: Houston’s Yordan Alvarez won the American League MVP and the Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong took the National League award, each unanimously and for the first time. With both Cy Young winners also unanimous, 2026 became the first season since the pitching award began in 1956 with four unanimous selections.

item.title: Pochettino to leave USMNT for Manchester United
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino will leave the U.S. men after the Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti and take charge of Manchester United on November 18. Reuters reports his contract runs through 2029. United sits 18th after its worst start in 40 years; Pochettino guided the U.S. to the 2026 World Cup round of 16.

item.title: NBC Sports voice Dan Hicks dies at 64
item.description: Dan Hicks, whose 35-year NBC career made him a familiar voice of golf, Olympic swimming and Notre Dame football, died after an acute illness. He called 16 Olympics, 27 U.S. Opens and Michael Phelps’ eight-gold performance in Beijing. NBC Sports president Rick Cordella called Hicks a cherished colleague and friend.

item.title: Spurs erase 22-point deficit for 10th consecutive victory
item.description: Victor Wembanyama scored 32 points as San Antonio rallied past Chicago 124-119 for its 10th straight win. Elsewhere, Houston ended Golden State’s eight-game streak after Stephen Curry left with abdominal soreness, while the Lakers became the NBA’s first 11-win team.

item.title: NCAA links repeated transfers to sharply lower graduation rates
item.description: New NCAA data covering about 36,000 athletes found that multiple transfers were generally associated with graduation rates 15 to 20 percentage points below those of athletes who stayed at one school. The gap reached 28 points in major-college football and was steepest for Black athletes.

item.title: United States withdraws from FIFA U-17 World Cup over safety concerns
item.description: U.S. Soccer pulled its boys’ national team from the 48-team tournament in Qatar, which is scheduled for Nov. 19 through Dec. 13. A letter to players cited current safety circumstances, making the Americans a late withdrawal from one of FIFA’s largest youth events.

item.title: NFL trade deadline reshapes contenders with Cousins, Allen and Downs deals
item.description: The Vikings reacquired Kirk Cousins from Las Vegas for a 2027 third-round pick, while San Francisco added Keenan Allen and Kansas City acquired Josh Downs. Buffalo, Denver and other contenders also made moves before Tuesday’s deadline, giving several playoff races a late-season jolt.

item.title: Georgia leads second CFP ranking as Notre Dame surges to No. 5
item.description: Georgia remained No. 1 in the committee’s second ranking, followed by Utah, Alabama and UCLA. Notre Dame made the biggest move near the top, jumping six places to No. 5, while Miami slipped to No. 7. The ranking begins to clarify the race for the expanded postseason field.

item.title: Ovechkin ties Capitals assist record on Hutson’s overtime winner
item.description: Alex Ovechkin set up Cole Hutson’s overtime goal in Washington’s 3-2 win at Ottawa, giving him 762 assists and a share of Nicklas Backstrom’s franchise record. The 20-year-old Hutson also assisted on the tying goal before scoring his first NHL overtime winner.

item.title: College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams in 2027
item.description: The CFP unanimously approved a 24-team field beginning in 2027-28, with first-round byes for the top eight seeds and 16 games played on campuses. ESPN will retain worldwide rights through 2031-32. The current 12-team format remains in place this season.

item.title: Cooper Flagg joins elite teenage company with 43-point night
item.description: Cooper Flagg scored 43 points with 10 rebounds and six assists as Dallas rallied past Indiana 125-122. The 19-year-old became only the second teenager in NBA history to produce at least 40 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a game.

item.title: McDavid extends point streak as historic assist run ends
item.description: Connor McDavid scored in Edmonton's 3-1 win over the Rangers, extending his season-opening point streak to 19 games. His assist streak ended at 18 games, tied with Adam Oates for the second-longest in NHL history behind Wayne Gretzky's 23-game run.
